# Subagent-Driven Development

Execute plan by dispatching fresh subagent per task, with two-stage review after each: spec compliance review first, then code quality review.

**Why subagents:** You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.

**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review (spec then quality) = high quality, fast iteration

**Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner between tasks. Execute all tasks from the plan without stopping. The only reasons to stop are: BLOCKED status you cannot resolve, ambiguity that genuinely prevents progress, or all tasks complete. "Should I continue?" prompts and progress summaries waste their time — they asked you to execute the plan, so execute it.

## When to Use

```dot
digraph when_to_use {
    "Have implementation plan?" [shape=diamond];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" [shape=diamond];
    "Stay in this session?" [shape=diamond];
    "subagent-driven-development" [shape=box];
    "executing-plans" [shape=box];
    "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [shape=box];

    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Tasks mostly independent?" [label="yes"];
    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Stay in this session?" [label="yes"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no - tightly coupled"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "subagent-driven-development" [label="yes"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "executing-plans" [label="no - parallel session"];
}
```

**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
- Same session (no context switch)
- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
- Two-stage review after each task: spec compliance first, then code quality
- Faster iteration (no human-in-loop between tasks)

## The Process

```dot
digraph process {
    rankdir=TB;

    subgraph cluster_per_task {
        label="Per Task";
        "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
        "Implementer subagent asks questions?" [shape=diamond];
        "Answer questions, provide context" [shape=box];
        "Implementer subagent implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" [shape=box];
        "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
        "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" [shape=diamond];
        "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" [shape=box];
        "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
        "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" [shape=diamond];
        "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" [shape=box];
        "Mark task complete in TodoWrite" [shape=box];
    }

    "Read plan, extract all tasks with full text, note context, create TodoWrite" [shape=box];
    "More tasks remain?" [shape=diamond];
    "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" [shape=box];
    "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch" [shape=box style=filled fillcolor=lightgreen];

    "Read plan, extract all tasks with full text, note context, create TodoWrite" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)";
    "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" -> "Implementer subagent asks questions?";
    "Implementer subagent asks questions?" -> "Answer questions, provide context" [label="yes"];
    "Answer questions, provide context" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)";
    "Implementer subagent asks questions?" -> "Implementer subagent implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" -> "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)";
    "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" -> "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?";
    "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" -> "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" -> "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="re-review"];
    "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" -> "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="yes"];
    "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" -> "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?";
    "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" -> "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" -> "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="re-review"];
    "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" -> "Mark task complete in TodoWrite" [label="yes"];
    "Mark task complete in TodoWrite" -> "More tasks remain?";
    "More tasks remain?" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" [label="yes"];
    "More tasks remain?" -> "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" [label="no"];
    "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" -> "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch";
}
```

## Model Selection

Use the least powerful model that can handle each role to conserve cost and increase speed.

**Mechanical implementation tasks** (isolated functions, clear specs, 1-2 files): use a fast, cheap model. Most implementation tasks are mechanical when the plan is well-specified.

**Integration and judgment tasks** (multi-file coordination, pattern matching, debugging): use a standard model.

**Architecture, design, and review tasks**: use the most capable available model.

**Task complexity signals:**
- Touches 1-2 files with a complete spec → cheap model
- Touches multiple files with integration concerns → standard model
- Requires design judgment or broad codebase understanding → most capable model

## Handling Implementer Status

Implementer subagents report one of four statuses. Handle each appropriately:

**DONE:** Proceed to spec compliance review.

**DONE_WITH_CONCERNS:** The implementer completed the work but flagged doubts. Read the concerns before proceeding. If the concerns are about correctness or scope, address them before review. If they're observations (e.g., "this file is getting large"), note them and proceed to review.

**NEEDS_CONTEXT:** The implementer needs information that wasn't provided. Provide the missing context and re-dispatch.

**BLOCKED:** The implementer cannot complete the task. Assess the blocker:
1. If it's a context problem, provide more context and re-dispatch with the same model
2. If the task requires more reasoning, re-dispatch with a more capable model
3. If the task is too large, break it into smaller pieces
4. If the plan itself is wrong, escalate to the human

**Never** ignore an escalation or force the same model to retry without changes. If the implementer said it's stuck, something needs to change.

## Prompt Templates

- `./implementer-prompt.md` - Dispatch implementer subagent
- `./spec-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch spec compliance reviewer subagent
- `./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent

## Example Workflow

```
You: I'm using Subagent-Driven Development to execute this plan.

[Read plan file once: docs/superpowers/plans/feature-plan.md]
[Extract all 5 tasks with full text and context]
[Create TodoWrite with all tasks]

Task 1: Hook installation script

[Get Task 1 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: "Before I begin - should the hook be installed at user or system level?"

You: "User level (~/.config/superpowers/hooks/)"

Implementer: "Got it. Implementing now..."
[Later] Implementer:
  - Implemented install-hook command
  - Added tests, 5/5 passing
  - Self-review: Found I missed --force flag, added it
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant - all requirements met, nothing extra

[Get git SHAs, dispatch code quality reviewer]
Code reviewer: Strengths: Good test coverage, clean. Issues: None. Approved.

[Mark Task 1 complete]

Task 2: Recovery modes

[Get Task 2 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: [No questions, proceeds]
Implementer:
  - Added verify/repair modes
  - 8/8 tests passing
  - Self-review: All good
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ❌ Issues:
  - Missing: Progress reporting (spec says "report every 100 items")
  - Extra: Added --json flag (not requested)

[Implementer fixes issues]
Implementer: Removed --json flag, added progress reporting

[Spec reviewer reviews again]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant now

[Dispatch code quality reviewer]
Code reviewer: Strengths: Solid. Issues (Important): Magic number (100)

[Implementer fixes]
Implementer: Extracted PROGRESS_INTERVAL constant

[Code reviewer reviews again]
Code reviewer: ✅ Approved

[Mark Task 2 complete]

...

[After all tasks]
[Dispatch final code-reviewer]
Final reviewer: All requirements met, ready to merge

Done!
```

## Advantages

**vs. Manual execution:**
- Subagents follow TDD naturally
- Fresh context per task (no confusion)
- Parallel-safe (subagents don't interfere)
- Subagent can ask questions (before AND during work)

**vs. Executing Plans:**
- Same session (no handoff)
- Continuous progress (no waiting)
- Review checkpoints automatic

**Efficiency gains:**
- No file reading overhead (controller provides full text)
- Controller curates exactly what context is needed
- Subagent gets complete information upfront
- Questions surfaced before work begins (not after)

**Quality gates:**
- Self-review catches issues before handoff
- Two-stage review: spec compliance, then code quality
- Review loops ensure fixes actually work
- Spec compliance prevents over/under-building
- Code quality ensures implementation is well-built

**Cost:**
- More subagent invocations (implementer + 2 reviewers per task)
- Controller does more prep work (extracting all tasks upfront)
- Review loops add iterations
- But catches issues early (cheaper than debugging later)

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent
- Skip reviews (spec compliance OR code quality)
- Proceed with unfixed issues
- Dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (conflicts)
- Make subagent read plan file (provide full text instead)
- Skip scene-setting context (subagent needs to understand where task fits)
- Ignore subagent questions (answer before letting them proceed)
- Accept "close enough" on spec compliance (spec reviewer found issues = not done)
- Skip review loops (reviewer found issues = implementer fixes = review again)
- Let implementer self-review replace actual review (both are needed)
- **Start code quality review before spec compliance is ✅** (wrong order)
- Move to next task while either review has open issues

**If subagent asks questions:**
- Answer clearly and completely
- Provide additional context if needed
- Don't rush them into implementation

**If reviewer finds issues:**
- Implementer (same subagent) fixes them
- Reviewer reviews again
- Repeat until approved
- Don't skip the re-review

**If subagent fails task:**
- Dispatch fix subagent with specific instructions
- Don't try to fix manually (context pollution)

## Integration

**Required workflow skills:**
- **superpowers:using-git-worktrees** - Ensures isolated workspace (creates one or verifies existing)
- **superpowers:writing-plans** - Creates the plan this skill executes
- **superpowers:requesting-code-review** - Code review template for reviewer subagents
- **superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch** - Complete development after all tasks

**Subagents should use:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - Subagents follow TDD for each task

**Alternative workflow:**
- **superpowers:executing-plans** - Use for parallel session instead of same-session execution
I'm using Subagent-Driven Development to execute this plan. Reading the three prompt templates first, then setting up.

# Implementer Subagent Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching an implementer subagent.

```
Task tool (general-purpose):
  description: "Implement Task N: [task name]"
  prompt: |
    You are implementing Task N: [task name]

    ## Task Description

    [FULL TEXT of task from plan - paste it here, don't make subagent read file]

    ## Context

    [Scene-setting: where this fits, dependencies, architectural context]

    ## Before You Begin

    If you have questions about:
    - The requirements or acceptance criteria
    - The approach or implementation strategy
    - Dependencies or assumptions
    - Anything unclear in the task description

    **Ask them now.** Raise any concerns before starting work.

    ## Your Job

    Once you're clear on requirements:
    1. Implement exactly what the task specifies
    2. Write tests (following TDD if task says to)
    3. Verify implementation works
    4. Commit your work
    5. Self-review (see below)
    6. Report back

    Work from: [directory]

    **While you work:** If you encounter something unexpected or unclear, **ask questions**.
    It's always OK to pause and clarify. Don't guess or make assumptions.

    ## Code Organization

    You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more
    reliable when files are focused. Keep this in mind:
    - Follow the file structure defined in the plan
    - Each file should have one clear responsibility with a well-defined interface
    - If a file you're creating is growing beyond the plan's intent, stop and report
      it as DONE_WITH_CONCERNS — don't split files on your own without plan guidance
    - If an existing file you're modifying is already large or tangled, work carefully
      and note it as a concern in your report
    - In existing codebases, follow established patterns. Improve code you're touching
      the way a good developer would, but don't restructure things outside your task.

    ## When You're in Over Your Head

    It is always OK to stop and say "this is too hard for me." Bad work is worse than
    no work. You will not be penalized for escalating.

    **STOP and escalate when:**
    - The task requires architectural decisions with multiple valid approaches
    - You need to understand code beyond what was provided and can't find clarity
    - You feel uncertain about whether your approach is correct
    - The task involves restructuring existing code in ways the plan didn't anticipate
    - You've been reading file after file trying to understand the system without progress

    **How to escalate:** Report back with status BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT. Describe
    specifically what you're stuck on, what you've tried, and what kind of help you need.
    The controller can provide more context, re-dispatch with a more capable model,
    or break the task into smaller pieces.

    ## Before Reporting Back: Self-Review

    Review your work with fresh eyes. Ask yourself:

    **Completeness:**
    - Did I fully implement everything in the spec?
    - Did I miss any requirements?
    - Are there edge cases I didn't handle?

    **Quality:**
    - Is this my best work?
    - Are names clear and accurate (match what things do, not how they work)?
    - Is the code clean and maintainable?

    **Discipline:**
    - Did I avoid overbuilding (YAGNI)?
    - Did I only build what was requested?
    - Did I follow existing patterns in the codebase?

    **Testing:**
    - Do tests actually verify behavior (not just mock behavior)?
    - Did I follow TDD if required?
    - Are tests comprehensive?

    If you find issues during self-review, fix them now before reporting.

    ## Report Format

    When done, report:
    - **Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT
    - What you implemented (or what you attempted, if blocked)
    - What you tested and test results
    - Files changed
    - Self-review findings (if any)
    - Any issues or concerns

    Use DONE_WITH_CONCERNS if you completed the work but have doubts about correctness.
    Use BLOCKED if you cannot complete the task. Use NEEDS_CONTEXT if you need
    information that wasn't provided. Never silently produce work you're unsure about.
```

out/

input.prompt:
You are applying a one-line follow-up fix to Task 1 of the Raven marketing-site rebuild.

## Background

Task 1 scaffolded `landing/` from the Tailwind Plus Salient template and configured Next.js for static export (`output: 'export'`). Code-quality review flagged that the `start` script in `landing/package.json` is dead weight: under static export, `next start` fails because there is no Node server runtime — Salient inherited that script from the default Next.js template where SSR is the norm.

## Fix

Edit `landing/package.json`. Replace the `start` script with one that previews the static build instead.

**Working directory:** `/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/.worktrees/landing-salient`

**Current scripts block:**

```json
"scripts": {
  "dev": "next dev",
  "build": "next build",
  "start": "next start",
  "lint": "next lint",
  "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
  "test": "playwright test"
}
```

**Change `start` to:**

```json
  "start": "npx serve out",
```

Leave all other keys untouched. Do not add `serve` to `devDependencies` — `npx` will resolve it on demand. (T17 adds `serve` as a real dev-dep for Playwright's webServer; until then `npx` is fine.)

## Steps

1. Edit `landing/package.json`: change exactly the `start` line.
2. Verify with `cd landing && cat package.json | python3 -c "import sys, json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['scripts'])"` — confirm the dict has the right `start` value and no other keys changed.
3. `npm run lint` (cheap sanity — should pass exactly as before).
4. Commit:

```bash
git add landing/package.json
git commit -m "fix(landing): replace dead 'next start' with 'npx serve out'

Static export has no Node server runtime; 'next start' would fail. Use
serve via npx so 'npm start' previews the actual production build."
```

5. Report back.

## Constraints

- Do NOT modify any other file.
- Do NOT push.
- Conventional commit, no `Co-Authored-By` trailer.

## Report format

- **Status:** DONE | BLOCKED
- The new commit SHA
- Confirm the only changed file is `landing/package.json` (`git diff --stat HEAD~1 HEAD`)

# Raven — Claude Code Instructions

## Pull Request Workflow

After creating a PR with `gh pr create`, **always** immediately queue it for auto-merge:

```bash
gh pr merge <PR_NUMBER> --auto --squash
```

This queues the PR to squash-merge automatically once all CI checks pass. Do not wait for CI — enqueue immediately after creation.

## Branch Naming

Use `type/descriptor` format:

| Type | When |
|------|------|
| `feat/` | New feature |
| `fix/` | Bug fix |
| `refactor/` | Code restructure, no behaviour change |
| `ci/` | CI/CD changes |
| `chore/` | Tooling, deps, config |
| `deps/` | Dependency bumps |

## Commit Style

- **No AI attribution** — do not add `Co-Authored-By:` trailers to any commit message
- Commits should appear as authored by the repo owner only

## Rules

- **Never push directly to `main`** — always use a PR
- **Squash merge only** — never regular merge or rebase-merge
- **Never use `--no-verify`** — all hooks must pass
- **Never amend published commits** — create new commits instead

## Memory: Stash MCP

Raven uses the Stash MCP server (`mcp__stash__*`) for persistent, cross-session memory. Treat it as the source of truth for project history, working rules, and decisions.

### Session-start protocol

1. `mcp__stash__init` — idempotent; ensures `/self` scaffold exists.
2. `mcp__stash__get_context` on `/projects/raven` — pick up any in-progress focus.
3. `mcp__stash__recall` with a query relevant to the user's first message, scoped to `/projects/raven` (recursive — covers all sub-namespaces). If the user's message is generic, also recall from `/users/jobinlawrance`.
4. If recall returns nothing on a topic, say so explicitly — do NOT answer from training data and pretend to remember.

### Namespace map

- `/users/jobinlawrance` — Jobin's profile, hardware, environment, payment/region constraints.
- `/projects/raven` — tech stack, edge-deployment requirements, compliance posture, Phase 2 features.
- `/projects/raven/auth` — Keycloak current state, Zitadel post-mortem, pluggable-auth direction.
- `/projects/raven/ai-worker` — Python gRPC service (port 50051), parsing, embeddings, RAG, voice.
- `/projects/raven/infra` — Compose variants, deployment, observability (OpenObserve + Beszel).
- `/projects/raven/milestones` — delivered + active queue (currently M9: #256, #257, #258).
- `/projects/raven/feedback` — standing rules: squash merge, no AI attribution, lint-before-push, testing gates, open-PR dependency, milestone protocol, respect tech choices.

### When to write

Call `mcp__stash__remember` (with the matching namespace) any time:

- A decision is finalised — technical, product, or process.
- The user states a preference, constraint, or correction.
- A milestone or issue changes state (started, blocked, shipped).
- You discover a non-obvious fact about the codebase, infra, or a third-party tool that future sessions would have to rediscover.
- You complete a session — write a one-line summary of what was done.

Use `mcp__stash__create_goal` for milestone-level intent and `mcp__stash__create_failure` for things that didn't work (e.g. the Zitadel decision). Use `mcp__stash__set_context` on `/projects/raven` when starting focused work, so the next session can pick up via `get_context`.

### Discipline

- Before writing to a namespace, verify it exists with `list_namespaces`. If missing, `create_namespace` first.
- Write complete self-contained sentences in `remember` — readable with zero prior context.
- Don't double-write the same fact to both `MEMORY.md` (built-in auto-memory) and Stash. Built-in memory holds terse rules loaded every turn; Stash holds project history, episodes, and goal/failure tracking queried on demand.

input.prompt:
Apply a one-line follow-up fix to Task 1 of the Raven marketing-site rebuild.

## Problem

`landing/package.json` defines `"lint": "next lint"`. Next.js 16 removed `next lint` (it was deprecated in 15). Reproducing locally:

```
$ cd landing && npm run lint
> next lint
Invalid project directory provided, no such directory: .../landing/lint
```

The Salient template shipped this script for Next 15. We're on Next 16 (per package.json's installed range). The fix is to invoke ESLint directly. Salient also shipped `eslint.config.mjs` (flat config) and `eslint-config-next` as a devDependency — both present in `landing/`.

## Fix

**Working directory:** `/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/.worktrees/landing-salient`

1. Edit `landing/package.json`. Change exactly the `lint` line:

   from:
   ```json
   "lint": "next lint",
   ```
   to:
   ```json
   "lint": "eslint .",
   ```

2. Verify scripts dict via `cd landing && cat package.json | python3 -c "import sys, json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['scripts'])"` — confirm only `lint` changed and the value is now `"eslint ."`.

3. Run `cd landing && npm run lint`. Expected: ESLint runs against the project (the Salient template code) and either reports no errors or reports specific lint findings (which is fine — we'll address them as part of T2 if any). The error must NOT be the previous "Invalid project directory" message.

   - If lint passes cleanly: great.
   - If lint reports findings on Salient code we haven't touched yet: that's expected upstream noise and not a blocker for this fix; report the count in the BlOCKED → DONE_WITH_CONCERNS path so I know.
   - If lint fails with config errors (not source-file findings), that's a blocker — STOP and report BLOCKED.

4. Commit:

   ```bash
   git add landing/package.json
   git commit -m "fix(landing): swap deprecated 'next lint' for direct eslint invocation

   next lint was removed in Next 16. The Salient template's eslint flat
   config (eslint.config.mjs) and eslint-config-next devDep are already
   in place, so 'eslint .' picks them up directly."
   ```

5. Report the new commit SHA and `git diff --stat HEAD~1 HEAD` (must show only `landing/package.json`).

## Constraints

- Do NOT modify any other file.
- Do NOT push.
- No `Co-Authored-By` trailer.

## Report format

- **Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED
- New commit SHA
- `git diff --stat HEAD~1 HEAD` output (one line)
- The lint result summary: "passed cleanly" or "passed with N warnings" or "failed: [reason]"

- Rewrote `landing/src/app/layout.tsx` to load Inter + Space Grotesk + JetBrains Mono via `next/font/google` (replacing Salient's Inter + Lexend), set Raven metadata defaults, and apply the three font CSS variables to `<html>`.

Spec compliance review already passed.

## Plan / requirements

Task 2 from `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-07-raven-marketing-site.md`. Spec at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-06-raven-marketing-site-design.md`.

- BASE_SHA: `e66e9ca2` (T1 commit + 2 fixes)
- HEAD_SHA: `2c307cba`
- Working dir: `/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/.worktrees/landing-salient`
- Files: `landing/public/fonts/ravenicons.woff2` (new binary), `landing/src/styles/tailwind.css` (rewrite), `landing/src/app/layout.tsx` (rewrite).

## What to look for

**Critical:** anything that breaks the build or violates the static-export deploy. Specifically:
- Is the woff2 path (`/fonts/ravenicons.woff2`) compatible with the `output: 'export'` + `trailingSlash: true` configuration? It should be — assets in `public/` are served at the same path regardless.
- Will `next/font/google` work in a static-export build? (Yes, since Next 13.2; fonts are downloaded at build time and self-hosted.)
- Does the CSP we'll define later in T16 (`font-src 'self'`) accommodate this? The `next/font/google` self-hosting and the `/fonts/ravenicons.woff2` are both same-origin, so yes.

- Naming: `--font-wordmark` vs `--font-display` — both make sense. Is the distinction useful enough to keep separate, or are they redundant?
- Whitespace, comment hygiene in `tailwind.css`.

- Does each new file have one clear responsibility? `tailwind.css` = theme + base + utility. `layout.tsx` = root layout + fonts + metadata. Two files, two responsibilities. Good or split?
- Are units decomposed so they can be understood independently? Yes for these.
- Is the file structure following the plan (per spec §4 file table)? Yes — `tailwind.css` and `layout.tsx` are exactly where they should be; `public/fonts/` is added (logged in the file table by the plan-update for T2).

## Report format

- **Strengths:** (one-liner each)
- **Issues:**
  - **Critical:** (would block merge)
  - **Important:** (should fix this round)
  - **Minor:** (nice to have)
- **Assessment:** APPROVED | CHANGES REQUESTED

Tight (~300 words). If everything's good, "approved, ship it" is fine.

- File responsibilities are clean: `tailwind.css` = theme + base styles + icon utility; `layout.tsx` = root shell + fonts + metadata.

**Issues:**

**Critical:** None.

**Important:**

- `--color-body` (`oklch(0.42 0 0)`) on `--color-bg` (`oklch(0.98 0.005 75)`) — the lightness delta is 0.56, which converts to roughly a 5.5:1 contrast ratio. That passes WCAG AA (4.5:1) for body text, so it is fine. However, `--color-body` is the default text color applied to the entire `<body>` including UI chrome. Any components that rely on this as placeholder or caption text will have barely-passing contrast. Consider bumping to `oklch(0.38 0 0)` to get more comfortable headroom.

- The `@tailwindcss/forms` plugin that existed in the Salient baseline was removed (visible in the diff). If any form component pages were inherited from Salient, they will lose their base form resets silently. This may be intentional (no forms on the landing), but it should be a conscious call, not an accidental deletion.

**Minor:**

- `--font-wordmark` is used only for `.raven-wordmark` (the icon font). It chains `'ravenicons'` → `var(--font-display)` as a text fallback, which means if the icon font fails to load the wordmark renders as display text. That's a reasonable degradation path but the distinction between `--font-wordmark` and `--font-display` is thin — it's really just "display + icon prefix." - Inline comments on colour tokens (`/* slate-950 */`) are helpful; consider adding one for `--color-border` which currently has none.

**Assessment: APPROVED**

No build-breaking issues. The `@tailwindcss/forms` removal warrants a quick confirmation that it's deliberate (no form pages on the landing), but it does not block merge. Everything else is clean. Ship it.

It contains four bird/wing SVGs at `ravenlogoassets/logo/Asset 7.svg`, `Asset 8.svg`, `Asset 11.svg`, `Asset 12.svg`. **There is no separate logo-full SVG** — the lockup is composed in JSX as ` + RAVEN` so the wordmark is rendered via the `ravenicons` font wired in T2. - [ ] **Step 1: Inspect the four bird-mark SVGs and pick one** ```bash for f in ravenlogoassets/logo/Asset\ {7,8,11,12}.svg; do echo "=== $f ===" head -3 "$f" done ``` Open each SVG in a browser or VS Code preview. **Pick the standalone wing/bird mark** (no circle background, no wordmark, no extra container shapes — just the bird in monochrome on transparent). Likely candidate: `Asset 7.svg` (smallest path-count file is usually the cleanest standalone). If unclear, check `git log -1 --format=%B 970252e0 -- 'ravenlogoassets/logo/'` for any context from the PR description, then default to the smallest file. - [ ] **Step 2: Copy the chosen bird SVG into the landing source tree** ```bash mkdir -p landing/src/images cp 'ravenlogoassets/logo/Asset 7.svg' landing/src/images/logo-mark.svg ``` (Substitute the chosen filename if you picked a different Asset. Filename in the destination must be `logo-mark.svg`.) - [ ] **Step 3: Replace `landing/src/components/Logo.tsx`** Overwrite the file: ```tsx import Image from 'next/image' import clsx from 'clsx' import logoMark from '@/images/logo-mark.svg' type LogoProps = { variant?: 'full' | 'mark' inverted?: boolean className?: string /** Tailwind height class for the bird mark. Defaults to `h-8`. */ markClassName?: string } export function Logo({ variant = 'full', inverted = false, className, markClassName = 'h-8 w-auto', }: LogoProps) { const mark = ( ) if (variant === 'mark') { return ( {mark} ) } return ( {mark} RAVEN ) } ``` The wordmark uses the `.raven-wordmark` utility (defined in T2's `tailwind.css`), which sets `font-family: ravenicons`. The literal text `RAVEN` then renders the brand wordmark. Inverted variant flips the bird to white via `invert` and switches the wordmark colour. - [ ] **Step 4: Write `landing/scripts/build-favicons.mjs`** ```js // One-shot favicon generator. Run manually after logo updates. // Usage: node scripts/build-favicons.mjs import sharp from 'sharp' import { promises as fs } from 'node:fs' import path from 'node:path' const SRC = path.resolve('src/images/logo-mark.svg') const PUB = path.resolve('public') const APP = path.resolve('src/app') const sizes = { 'favicon-16x16.png': 16, 'favicon-32x32.png': 32, 'apple-touch-icon.png': 180, 'android-chrome-192x192.png': 192, 'android-chrome-512x512.png': 512, } async function main() { const svg = await fs.readFile(SRC) for (const [name, size] of Object.entries(sizes)) { const out = path.join(PUB, name) await sharp(svg, { density: 384 }) .resize(size, size, { fit: 'contain', background: { r: 0, g: 0, b: 0, alpha: 0 } }) .png() .toFile(out) console.log('wrote', out) } // App-router convention: src/app/favicon.ico (binary 32×32 PNG renamed; Next handles it). await sharp(svg, { density: 384 }) .resize(32, 32, { fit: 'contain' }) .toFormat('png') .toFile(path.join(APP, 'favicon.ico')) console.log('wrote', path.join(APP, 'favicon.ico')) await fs.writeFile( path.join(PUB, 'site.webmanifest'), JSON.stringify( { name: 'Raven', short_name: 'Raven', icons: [ { src: '/android-chrome-192x192.png', sizes: '192x192', type: 'image/png' }, { src: '/android-chrome-512x512.png', sizes: '512x512', type: 'image/png' }, ], theme_color: '#0a0a0a', background_color: '#fafaf9', display: 'standalone', }, null, 2, ), ) console.log('wrote site.webmanifest') } main().catch((err) => { console.error(err) process.exit(1) }) ``` - [ ] **Step 5: Run the favicon script** ```bash cd landing && node scripts/build-favicons.mjs ``` Expected: prints 7 "wrote" lines, no errors. - [ ] **Step 6: Smoke — dev server, check Logo renders** ```bash npm run dev ``` Expected: existing pages still render; the Salient `Header` (which already uses ``) shows the Raven wing mark instead of TaxPal's logo. Stop dev server. - [ ] **Step 7: Lint + typecheck** ```bash npm run lint && npm run typecheck ``` - [ ] **Step 8: Commit** ```bash git add landing/src/images/logo-mark.svg \ landing/src/components/Logo.tsx landing/scripts/build-favicons.mjs \ landing/public/favicon-16x16.png landing/public/favicon-32x32.png \ landing/public/apple-touch-icon.png \ landing/public/android-chrome-192x192.png landing/public/android-chrome-512x512.png \ landing/public/site.webmanifest landing/src/app/favicon.ico git commit -m "feat(landing): wire Raven bird mark, ravenicons wordmark, favicons Vendors the bird mark SVG from ravenlogoassets/logo/ into the landing source tree. The Logo component composes the lockup in JSX as bird mark + a span using the .raven-wordmark utility (font-family: ravenicons) so the literal text 'RAVEN' renders the brand wordmark. A one-shot scripts/build-favicons.mjs generates the favicon family from logo-mark.svg via sharp." ``` ## Context You are working in a git worktree of the Raven monorepo: - **Working directory:** `/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/.worktrees/landing-salient` - **Branch:** `feat/landing-salient-rebuild` - **Plan:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-07-raven-marketing-site.md` (T3 above) T1 scaffolded `landing/` from Salient. T2 wired the Raven palette + fonts (Inter / Space Grotesk / JetBrains Mono via `next/font`, plus the `ravenicons` font face vendored at `landing/public/fonts/ravenicons.woff2`). The `.raven-wordmark` utility in `landing/src/styles/tailwind.css` exposes `font-family: ravenicons; letter-spacing: 0.05em;` — that's what the Logo component leans on for the wordmark. `sharp` is already a devDependency from the Salient template (it ships with it for `next/image` optimization), so the favicon script can run as-is — no `npm install` needed before running. Salient's `Header.tsx` (still in its original form) already imports `` at the top, so the dev-server smoke test will exercise the Logo component automatically. The Salient `Logo.tsx` currently exports the TaxPal accounting-software wordmark as a literal `

content.text: Now I have everything I need. Here is the review: --- ## Code-Quality Review — Task 3 (Brand Assets Wiring) ### Strengths - **Clean prop API.** Four props, sensible defaults, all typed. `clsx` used correctly throughout. - **A11y is correct.** `aria-label="Raven"` on the wrapper span gives screen readers the accessible name; `alt=""` + `aria-hidden="true"` on the inner `` marks it decorative. No double-labelling — the outer label is the single source, the inner attributes suppress the redundant element. This is the textbook correct pattern. - **favicon.ico placement is right.** `src/app/favicon.ico` is the Next.js App Router convention; Next auto-serves it as `/favicon.ico`. Correct. - **`density: 384` is well-chosen.** Sharp's SVG rasteriser uses density (DPI) to determine the pixel grid before resizing. 384 DPI produces a 384×384 native raster from a nominally 1-inch SVG, which then scales down cleanly to 16×16 without loss. No blurriness concern. - **`favicon.ico` write is honest.** `.toFormat('png')` forces PNG encoding before the `.ico` extension; comment accurately describes it. Modern browsers and Next handle it fine. - **`site.webmanifest` colour values.** `#0a0a0a` ≈ `oklch(0.18 0 0)` and `#fafaf9` ≈ `oklch(0.98 0.005 75)` — within a visible rounding error. Not a bug. - **Error handling in script.** `main().catch(err => { console.error(err); process.exit(1) })` ensures non-zero exit on failure — CI-safe. --- ### Issues **Important — Baseline alignment (`full` variant)** `items-baseline` on the flex container tries to align the wordmark text's baseline with the image's baseline. But `` (an `` element) has its baseline at its bottom edge by default, not its optical centre. At `h-8` (32 px) bird + `text-2xl` wordmark, the bird will sit lower than intended — the bottom of the bird will align with the text baseline rather than the bird's optical midpoint aligning with the cap-height. The correct fix is `items-center` (or add `self-center` to the image), which is what virtually every logo lockup does. input.prompt:
You are reviewing whether an implementation matches its specification. Verify by reading actual code, not trusting the report.

## What Was Requested

Task 4 of the Raven marketing-site rebuild plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-07-raven-marketing-site.md`): rebrand the Header, Footer, and Button components.

Required deliverables (verbatim from plan):

1. **Replace `landing/src/components/Button.tsx`** with a discriminated-union ButtonProps that supports:
   - `variant: 'solid' | 'outline'` (default `'solid'`)
   - `color: 'accent' | 'ink'` (default `'accent'`)
   - `href?: string` switching between `<Link>` and `<button>`
   - Style tokens drawn from CSS vars `--color-accent`, `--color-accent-hover`, `--color-ink`, `--color-body`, `--color-border`
   - Uses `clsx`. Named export `Button`.

2. **Replace `landing/src/components/Header.tsx`** — `'use client'` directive, Headless UI Popover for mobile menu, four nav links: `/#features`, `/pricing`, `/self-host`, `/about`. GitHub link to `https://github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven`. Primary CTA "Self-host in 5 min" → `/self-host`. Logo: `mark` variant on mobile (`md:hidden`), `full` variant on desktop (`hidden md:inline-flex`). Container wraps the nav. Sticky-pad `py-6`.

3. **Replace `landing/src/components/Footer.tsx`** — dark ink background, inverted Logo mark (h-10), 5-link row (Features / Pricing / Self-host / About / GitHub), GitHub icon link in lower-right, Ravencloak copyright with current year.

4. **Inspect `Container.tsx` and `NavLink.tsx`**. Patch any `text-slate-*` / `text-blue-*` literals. Otherwise leave alone.

5. Single commit on `feat/landing-salient-rebuild` with title `feat(landing): rebrand Header/Footer/Button with Raven nav and palette`. No `Co-Authored-By`.

6. **Out of scope** — must NOT have happened: changes to `Hero.tsx`, `PrimaryFeatures.tsx`, `SecondaryFeatures.tsx`, `Faqs.tsx`, `Logo.tsx`, `tailwind.css`, `app/layout.tsx`, `app/page.tsx`, `Container.tsx` (unless brand colours found), or any file outside `landing/`. Push or PR creation: forbidden.

7. **Implementer flagged two deviations you must judge:**
   a. **Headless UI v2 transition API**: The plan's `Header.tsx` snippet used `<Transition>` (v1 API). Salient actually ships HUI v2.2.10, where `Transition` was removed and replaced with the data-attribute pattern (`PopoverPanel transition data-closed:opacity-0 …`). Implementer adapted to v2's idiom. **Verify they used the correct v2 pattern** (props like `transition`, `data-[closed]:*`, etc., NOT the v1 `<Transition>` wrapper).
   b. **Collateral edits to `CallToAction.tsx` and `Pricing.tsx`**: My new Button union dropped Salient's `color="white"` variant. The two unmodified Salient files used `color="white"` and would fail TypeScript without a patch. Implementer changed both to `color="accent"`. **Verify the change is exactly that minimal one-prop swap** and didn't accidentally rewrite anything else in those files. (Both files are scheduled for full replacement in T8 and T10 — so this patch is throwaway, but it must be small.)

## What Implementer Claims They Built

- Status DONE; commit `ade2456e`.
- 6 files: Button.tsx, Header.tsx, Footer.tsx, NavLink.tsx (slate→tokens), CallToAction.tsx (color="white"→"accent"), Pricing.tsx (same).
- Container.tsx: inspected, untouched.
- HUI v2 transition pattern used.
- Lint + typecheck pass; dev server served 200; grep confirmed `raven-wordmark`, "Self-host in 5 min", "ravencloak", "GitHub" in markup.

## CRITICAL: Do Not Trust the Report

Verify everything independently.

## Verification checklist

Working dir: `/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/.worktrees/landing-salient`.

1. `git log --oneline -2 feat/landing-salient-rebuild` — confirm `ade2456e` is HEAD with the spec'd title and no `Co-Authored-By` trailer (full message via `git log -1 --format=%B`).

2. `git diff --stat HEAD~1 HEAD` — confirm exactly 6 files changed and they are the ones reported. Anything outside `landing/src/components/` or with a different name is a violation.

3. Read `landing/src/components/Button.tsx`. Spot-check:
   - Has discriminated union `ButtonProps` with `variant` and `color` keys.
   - `solid.accent` style references `bg-[var(--color-accent)]` and `hover:bg-[var(--color-accent-hover)]`.
   - `solid.ink` references `bg-[var(--color-ink)]`.
   - `outline.accent` references `border-[var(--color-accent)]` and `text-[var(--color-accent)]`.
   - `outline.ink` references `border-[var(--color-border)]` and `text-[var(--color-ink)]`.
   - Renders `<Link>` when `href` defined, `<button>` otherwise.
   - Default `variant ?? 'solid'`, `color ?? 'accent'`.

4. Read `landing/src/components/Header.tsx`. Verify:
   - First line is `'use client'`.
   - Imports the four expected items + Logo + Container + Button + NavLink + Headless UI primitives.
   - Has `const REPO_URL = 'https://github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven'`.
   - Four `<NavLink>` entries with the four hrefs (`/#features`, `/pricing`, `/self-host`, `/about`).
   - The four mobile `<MobileNavLink>` entries match the same four hrefs + GitHub.
   - Logo composition: `<Logo variant="mark" markClassName="h-8 w-auto md:hidden" />` then `<Logo variant="full" markClassName="h-8 w-auto" className="hidden md:inline-flex" />`.
   - GitHub button: `<Button href={REPO_URL} variant="outline" color="ink" className="hidden md:inline-flex">GitHub</Button>`.
   - Self-host CTA: `<Button href="/self-host">Self-host in 5 min</Button>`.
   - **HUI v2 verification:** Look for the v2 idiom — `transition` prop on `PopoverPanel`/`PopoverBackdrop`, classes like `data-closed:opacity-0`, `data-enter:duration-150` etc. Verify there is NO `<Transition>` JSX element wrapping `PopoverPanel` (that's v1, would be wrong).

5. Read `landing/src/components/Footer.tsx`. Verify dark `bg-[var(--color-ink)]`, inverted Logo mark via `<Logo variant="mark" inverted markClassName="h-10 w-auto" className="mx-auto" />`, the 5-link `<ul>` matches the spec'd hrefs, current-year copyright using `new Date().getFullYear()`, "Ravencloak" word in the copyright string. No leftover Salient text.

6. Read `landing/src/components/NavLink.tsx`. Verify it no longer references `text-slate-*` or `text-blue-*` literals — should reference CSS tokens via `var(--color-*)` or be visually neutral. The exact Tailwind classes used can vary slightly; what matters is no Salient brand-colour literals remain.

7. Read `landing/src/components/Container.tsx`. Verify it was NOT modified in this commit (`git diff HEAD~1 HEAD -- landing/src/components/Container.tsx` produces no output).

8. Verify the collateral edits are TINY:
   - `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD -- landing/src/components/CallToAction.tsx`: should show only `color="white"` → `color="accent"` (one or two lines), nothing else. Anything more is a violation.
   - `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD -- landing/src/components/Pricing.tsx`: same — only the `color="white"` → `color="accent"` swaps. Could be multiple occurrences but each one a single prop change.
   - **Critically:** verify the implementer did NOT pre-emptively rewrite content in those files, change copy, restructure, etc.

9. Verify the build still works: `cd landing && rm -rf .next out && npm run build 2>&1 | tail -8`. Must exit 0.

10. Verify lint and typecheck still pass: `cd landing && npm run lint && npm run typecheck`. Both must exit 0.

11. Verify zero modifications outside the in-scope set:
    - `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD -- landing/src/components/Hero.tsx landing/src/components/PrimaryFeatures.tsx landing/src/components/SecondaryFeatures.tsx landing/src/components/Faqs.tsx landing/src/components/Logo.tsx landing/src/components/Testimonials.tsx landing/src/components/Fields.tsx landing/src/components/SlimLayout.tsx` — all empty.
    - `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD -- landing/src/styles/ landing/src/app/ landing/public/ landing/scripts/` — all empty.
    - `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD ':(exclude)landing/'` — empty.

## Report

Return:
- ✅ Spec compliant (one-liner per item)
- ❌ Issues found: file/line/output evidence

~400 words.

input.prompt:
Apply a small follow-up fix to T4's Button component.

## Problem

`landing/src/components/Button.tsx` destructures only `className` from props, then spreads the remaining `...props` (which still includes `variant` and `color`) into a `<button>` or `<Link>`. React forwards unknown props to the DOM and emits a console warning:

> Warning: React does not recognize the `variant` prop on a DOM element.

## Fix

**Working directory:** `/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/.worktrees/landing-salient`

In `landing/src/components/Button.tsx`, change the `Button` function to destructure `variant` and `color` out of `props` before spreading the rest:

Replace this block:
```tsx
export function Button({ className, ...props }: ButtonProps) {
  const variant = props.variant ?? 'solid'
  const color = props.color ?? 'accent'
  className = clsx(
    baseStyles[variant],
    variant === 'solid'
      ? variantStyles.solid[color as keyof typeof variantStyles.solid]
      : variantStyles.outline[color as keyof typeof variantStyles.outline],
    className,
  )
  return typeof props.href === 'undefined' ? (
    <button className={className} {...(props as React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'>)} />
  ) : (
    <Link className={className} {...(props as React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof Link>)} />
  )
}
```

with:
```tsx
export function Button({
  className,
  variant: variantProp,
  color: colorProp,
  ...rest
}: ButtonProps) {
  const variant = variantProp ?? 'solid'
  const color = colorProp ?? 'accent'
  className = clsx(
    baseStyles[variant],
    variant === 'solid'
      ? variantStyles.solid[color as keyof typeof variantStyles.solid]
      : variantStyles.outline[color as keyof typeof variantStyles.outline],
    className,
  )
  return typeof rest.href === 'undefined' ? (
    <button className={className} {...(rest as React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'>)} />
  ) : (
    <Link className={className} {...(rest as React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof Link>)} />
  )
}
```

## Steps

1. Edit `landing/src/components/Button.tsx` per above.
2. Verify lint + typecheck still pass:
   ```bash
   cd landing && npm run lint && npm run typecheck
   ```
3. Quick smoke: `cd landing && rm -rf .next out && npm run build 2>&1 | tail -5` — must exit 0.
4. Commit:
   ```bash
   git add landing/src/components/Button.tsx
   git commit -m "fix(landing): destructure variant/color out of Button props before DOM spread

   Previously Button spread the full props (including variant and color)
   into <button>/<Link>, causing React to warn 'unknown prop on DOM
   element'. Pull both out explicitly so only valid HTML attributes
   reach the underlying element."
   ```

## Constraints

- Do NOT modify any other file.
- Do NOT push.
- Conventional commit, no `Co-Authored-By` trailer.

## Report

- **Status:** DONE | BLOCKED
- New commit SHA
- `git diff --stat HEAD~1 HEAD` (one line)
- Lint + typecheck + build result

# Raven — Claude Code Instructions

## Pull Request Workflow

After creating a PR with `gh pr create`, **always** immediately queue it for auto-merge:

```bash
gh pr merge <PR_NUMBER> --auto --squash
```

This queues the PR to squash-merge automatically once all CI checks pass. Do not wait for CI — enqueue immediately after creation.

## Branch Naming

Use `type/descriptor` format:

| Type | When |
|------|------|
| `feat/` | New feature |
| `fix/` | Bug fix |
| `refactor/` | Code restructure, no behaviour change |
| `ci/` | CI/CD changes |
| `chore/` | Tooling, deps, config |
| `deps/` | Dependency bumps |

## Commit Style

- **No AI attribution** — do not add `Co-Authored-By:` trailers to any commit message
- Commits should appear as authored by the repo owner only

## Rules

- **Never push directly to `main`** — always use a PR
- **Squash merge only** — never regular merge or rebase-merge
- **Never use `--no-verify`** — all hooks must pass
- **Never amend published commits** — create new commits instead

## Memory: Stash MCP

Raven uses the Stash MCP server (`mcp__stash__*`) for persistent, cross-session memory. Treat it as the source of truth for project history, working rules, and decisions.

### Session-start protocol

1. `mcp__stash__init` — idempotent; ensures `/self` scaffold exists.
2. `mcp__stash__get_context` on `/projects/raven` — pick up any in-progress focus.
3. `mcp__stash__recall` with a query relevant to the user's first message, scoped to `/projects/raven` (recursive — covers all sub-namespaces). If the user's message is generic, also recall from `/users/jobinlawrance`.
4. If recall returns nothing on a topic, say so explicitly — do NOT answer from training data and pretend to remember.

### Namespace map

- `/users/jobinlawrance` — Jobin's profile, hardware, environment, payment/region constraints.
- `/projects/raven` — tech stack, edge-deployment requirements, compliance posture, Phase 2 features.
- `/projects/raven/auth` — Keycloak current state, Zitadel post-mortem, pluggable-auth direction.
- `/projects/raven/ai-worker` — Python gRPC service (port 50051), parsing, embeddings, RAG, voice.
- `/projects/raven/infra` — Compose variants, deployment, observability (OpenObserve + Beszel).
- `/projects/raven/milestones` — delivered + active queue (currently M9: #256, #257, #258).
- `/projects/raven/feedback` — standing rules: squash merge, no AI attribution, lint-before-push, testing gates, open-PR dependency, milestone protocol, respect tech choices.

### When to write

Call `mcp__stash__remember` (with the matching namespace) any time:

- A decision is finalised — technical, product, or process.
- The user states a preference, constraint, or correction.
- A milestone or issue changes state (started, blocked, shipped).
- You discover a non-obvious fact about the codebase, infra, or a third-party tool that future sessions would have to rediscover.
- You complete a session — write a one-line summary of what was done.

Use `mcp__stash__create_goal` for milestone-level intent and `mcp__stash__create_failure` for things that didn't work (e.g. the Zitadel decision). Use `mcp__stash__set_context` on `/projects/raven` when starting focused work, so the next session can pick up via `get_context`.

### Discipline

- Before writing to a namespace, verify it exists with `list_namespaces`. If missing, `create_namespace` first.
- Write complete self-contained sentences in `remember` — readable with zero prior context.
- Don't double-write the same fact to both `MEMORY.md` (built-in auto-memory) and Stash. Built-in memory holds terse rules loaded every turn; Stash holds project history, episodes, and goal/failure tracking queried on demand.

import { type Metadata } from 'next'

import { CallToAction } from '@/components/CallToAction'
import { Faqs } from '@/components/Faqs'
import { Footer } from '@/components/Footer'
import { Header } from '@/components/Header'
import { Hero } from '@/components/Hero'
import { PricingTeaser } from '@/components/PricingTeaser'
import { PrimaryFeatures } from '@/components/PrimaryFeatures'
import { SecondaryFeatures } from '@/components/SecondaryFeatures'

export const metadata: Metadata = {
  alternates: { canonical: 'https://raven.ravencloak.org/' },
}

export default function Home() {
  return (
    <>
      <Header />
      <main>
        <Hero />
        <PrimaryFeatures />
        <SecondaryFeatures />

name: Deploy Landing to Cloudflare Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "landing/**"
      - ".github/workflows/landing.yml"

concurrency:
  group: landing-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions: {}

jobs:
  deploy:
    name: Deploy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      deployments: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Deploy to Cloudflare Pages
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
        if: env.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN != ''
        uses: cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3
        with:
          apiToken: ${{ env.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          accountId: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          command: pages deploy landing --project-name=raven-landing --branch=main --commit-dirty=true

name: Deploy Landing to Cloudflare Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "landing/**"
      - ".github/workflows/landing.yml"
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "landing/**"
      - ".github/workflows/landing.yml"

concurrency:
  group: landing-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions: {}

jobs:
  build-and-deploy:
    name: Build & Deploy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      deployments: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "npm"
          cache-dependency-path: landing/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: landing
        run: npm ci

      - name: Lint
        working-directory: landing
        run: npm run lint

      # Build before typecheck: `next build` regenerates `next-env.d.ts`
      # (which is gitignored), and `tsc --noEmit` depends on the type
      # references it declares. Build also runs its own TS check on
      # everything reachable from app/, so this catches type errors first.
      - name: Build
        working-directory: landing
        run: npm run build

      - name: Typecheck
        working-directory: landing
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        working-directory: landing
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Smoke tests
        working-directory: landing
        env:
          CI: "true"
        run: npm test

      - name: Upload Playwright report on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: landing/playwright-report/
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Deploy to Cloudflare Pages
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
        if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && env.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN != ''
        uses: cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3
        with:
          apiToken: ${{ env.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          accountId: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          command: pages deploy landing/out --project-name=raven-landing --branch=main --commit-dirty=true
          gitHubToken: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

| Parallel (3 groups) | A: 5 home-page section components · B: /pricing + /self-host + /about + 404 · C: SEO + security headers — merged back into the feature branch with zero conflicts (disjoint file sets) |
| Serial tail | Assemble `app/page.tsx` + delete unused Salient bits · Playwright smoke + visual baselines · CI workflow rewrite · push + PR + auto-merge |

**Notable fixes / lessons that landed inline (not in original spec):**
- Salient ships `next start` and `next lint` but Next 16 removed `next lint` and `next start` is broken under static export — swapped to `eslint .` and `npx serve out`.
- Headless UI v2 dropped the `<Transition>` wrapper component; Group B/A used the `transition` boolean prop + `data-[closed]:*` attribute pattern instead.
- The OG image route needed three production-export fixes: `export const dynamic = 'force-static'`, vendoring the **TTF** of ravenicons (satori rejects WOFF2), and switching `oklch()` colour values to hex (satori only supports hex/rgb/named).
- CI ordering had to be **install → lint → build → typecheck** (not the inverse): `next-env.d.ts` is gitignored and only regenerated by `next build`, so `tsc --noEmit` before build sees ghost-missing module declarations for `*.svg` / `*.png` imports.
- Visual snapshot tests gated to local-only via `test.skip(!!process.env.CI, …)` because font rendering across macOS/Linux/Windows would false-positive baselines.

**After auto-merge** the existing `landing.yml` runs against main, which builds and deploys to the `raven-landing` Cloudflare Pages project — so `raven.ravencloak.org` cuts over automatically. The CF Pages PR preview URL on #412 will let you click through the new site before merge.

**Cleanup available, not done** (destructive — say the word): the 3 group worktrees (`feat/landing-group-{a,b,c}` in `.worktrees/landing-salient-{a,b,c}`) are no longer needed; `git worktree remove` + `git branch -D` once you're satisfied the merged work is right.

content.content:
codeql.yml
---
name: CodeQL

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '23 6 * * 1'

permissions: {}

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Detect relevant changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      code: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.code }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@8e8c483db84b4bee98b60c0593521ed34d9990e8  # v6.0.1

      - name: Filter paths
        id: filter
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@fbd0ab8f3e69293af611ebaee6363fc25e6d187d  # v4.0.1
        with:
          filters: |
            code:
              - '**/*.go'
              - '**/*.py'
              - '**/*.ts'
              - '**/*.tsx'
              - '**/*.js'
              - '**/*.vue'
              - 'go.mod'
              - 'go.sum'
              - 'frontend/package.json'
              - 'frontend/bun.lock'
              - 'ai-worker/pyproject.toml'
              - 'ai-worker/requirements*.txt'
              - '.github/workflows/codeql.yml'

  analyze:
    name: Analyze (${{ matrix.language }})
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true' || github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      security-events: write
      contents: read
      actions: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - language: go
            build-mode: autobuild
          - language: python
            build-mode: none
          - language: javascript-typescript
            build-mode: none
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@8e8c483db84b4bee98b60c0593521ed34d9990e8  # v6.0.1

      - name: Setup Go
        if: matrix.language == 'go'
        uses: actions/setup-go@4a3601121dd01d1626a1e23e37211e3254c1c06c  # v6.4.0
        with:
          go-version: '1.26.2'
          cache: true

      - name: Initialize CodeQL
        uses: github/codeql-action/init@95e58e9a2cdfd71adc6e0353d5c52f41a045d225  # v4
        with:
          languages: ${{ matrix.language }}
          build-mode: ${{ matrix.build-mode }}
          queries: security-extended

content.text:
Found the root cause. It's a **branch-protection misconfig**, not a workflow problem.

Branch protection on `main` has two redundant-but-differently-shaped CodeQL requirements:

```
required checks:
  - Gate              (app_id=15368, GitHub Actions)   ← satisfied by both workflows
  - CodeQL / Gate     (app_id=None, any source)        ← stuck "Expected"
```

Two different workflows emit a job named `Gate`:
- `CodeQL` workflow → gate job (currently passing on `0eb04985`)
- `CI Required` workflow → gate job (also passing)

Both post their result as a **check_run** with the bare name `Gate` — that satisfies the first requirement.

The second requirement, `CodeQL / Gate`, is a legacy **status-context** matcher that expects a check whose context name is literally `CodeQL / Gate`. The CodeQL workflow doesn't emit one — it only emits a check_run. So GitHub keeps showing it as "Expected — Waiting for status to be reported", forever.

This is the kind of duplication that crept in when commit `53d950ac ci(codeql): add Gate job for required-check semantics (#348)` reshaped the CodeQL gate; the old context name never got pruned from branch protection.

**Two ways to fix:**

- **A) Drop `CodeQL / Gate` from required checks** (recommended). It's redundant with the generic `Gate` requirement that's already passing. One API call:
  ```
  gh api -X PATCH repos/ravencloak-org/Raven/branches/main/protection/required_status_checks \
    -f 'checks=[{"context":"Gate","app_id":15368},{"context":"DCO Sign-off","app_id":15368},{"context":"Gitleaks","app_id":15368}]'
  ```
- **B) Make the CodeQL workflow emit a legacy status context** named `CodeQL / Gate` alongside the check_run (extra `actions/github-script` step calling `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/statuses/{sha}`). More moving parts, no real benefit over A.

I won't touch branch protection without you explicitly OKing it — modifying `main`'s required-checks list is a shared-infra change and I'd rather you authorise the exact edit. Want me to run the (A) command?

**No, no hooks were created** — and the existing setup is actively misconfigured:

- `git config core.hooksPath` is set to **`.githooks`**, but that directory **doesn't exist**. So hooks never run.
- The `.git/hooks/{commit-msg,prepare-commit-msg,post-commit,pre-push}` files dated 2026-03-27 are dead — they sit at the default path that's overridden by `core.hooksPath`.
- `format.signOff` is unset both locally and globally — that's why every commit on this PR was missing `Signed-off-by:` until I rebased with `--signoff` after the fact.

**Cleanest fix is one command, no scripts:**

```bash
git config --local format.signOff true     # in this repo only
# or
git config --global format.signOff true    # everywhere on this machine
```

That makes `git commit` automatically append `Signed-off-by: <git user.name> <git user.email>` to every commit message — same effect as remembering `-s` every time, without the discipline tax. CI is happy, no hook script to maintain.

Want me to set it `--local` for this repo? (Or `--global` if you'd rather have it on by default for every repo on this machine — sensible since DCO is increasingly the norm in OSS.)

# Resilience Layer for Raven Go API — Design

**Date:** 2026-05-08
**Status:** Approved (awaiting implementation plan)
**Owner:** Jobin Lawrance
**Target branch:** `feat/resilience-layer` (worktree, from latest `origin/main`)

## Context

The Raven Go API today has scattered `context.WithTimeout` usage in `internal/middleware/ratelimit.go`, `internal/service/security.go`, `internal/service/billing.go`, and `internal/repository/semantic_cache.go`, but no consistent discipline at the boundaries that matter most:

- **AI worker gRPC client** (`internal/grpc/client.go`) — has fault-injection tests in `internal/integration/grpc_fault_test.go`, but no circuit breaker. A stalled Python worker today will pile up goroutines on the API process until OOM.
- **`http.Server` in `cmd/api/main.go`** — uses `gin.Default()` with no `ReadTimeout`/`WriteTimeout`/`IdleTimeout`/`ReadHeaderTimeout` set on the underlying `http.Server`. Go's defaults are zero, which means a slow client can hold a connection forever (slowloris class).
- **Per-route deadlines** — Gin handlers do not enforce per-route context budgets. A handler that forgets `ctx.WithTimeout` can run indefinitely.
- **Asynq handlers** — task handlers do not consistently apply per-task deadlines, so a stuck handler holds a worker slot indefinitely.

No `gobreaker` / `failsafe` / `circuitbreaker` imports exist anywhere in production code today.

## Goals

1. Bound every external call by an explicit deadline.
2. Trip a circuit breaker on the AI-worker gRPC client to prevent cascading failure.
3. Harden the `http.Server` against slowloris-class hangs.
4. Enforce a per-route Gin context deadline so no handler runs unbounded.
5. Apply consistent per-task deadlines in Asynq handlers.
6. Add a CI compliance gate that fails when new code introduces external calls without context deadlines.

## Non-Goals (deferred to follow-up issues)

- Bulkhead semaphores (per-dependency goroutine caps).

# Resilience Layer Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Add bounded-deadline + circuit-breaker resilience to the Raven Go API across the AI-worker gRPC client, `http.Server`, per-route Gin handlers, and Asynq job handlers — with unit + integration tests and a CI compliance gate.

**Architecture:** New `internal/resilience/` package owns reusable primitives (`Policy`, breaker adapter, gRPC interceptor, HTTP RoundTripper). New `internal/middleware/deadline.go` enforces per-route context deadlines. `cmd/api/main.go` wires explicit `http.Server` timeouts and the Deadline middleware. `.golangci.yml` adds `noctx` + `contextcheck` as blocking lint gates.

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.22+, Gin, `google.golang.org/grpc`, `github.com/sony/gobreaker`, `github.com/hibiken/asynq`, `golangci-lint v2`.

**Spec:** [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-08-resilience-design.md`](../specs/2026-05-08-resilience-design.md)

## Parallel-execution map

Tasks group into phases. Tasks within a phase can run in parallel (disjoint file ownership). Tasks across phases are sequential.

| Phase | Tasks | Parallelizable | Notes |

| 0 — Bootstrap | 1 | no | Worktree + dep + survey |
| 1 — Primitives | 2, 3, 6, 7, 8 | **yes (5 agents)** | All write disjoint files |

# Resilience Layer for Raven Go API — Design

**Date:** 2026-05-08
**Status:** Approved (awaiting implementation plan)
**Owner:** Jobin Lawrance
**Target branch:** `feat/resilience-layer` (worktree, from latest `origin/main`)

## Context

The Raven Go API today has scattered `context.WithTimeout` usage in `internal/middleware/ratelimit.go`, `internal/service/security.go`, `internal/service/billing.go`, and `internal/repository/semantic_cache.go`, but no consistent discipline at the boundaries that matter most:

- **AI worker gRPC client** (`internal/grpc/client.go`) — has fault-injection tests in `internal/integration/grpc_fault_test.go`, but no circuit breaker. A stalled Python worker today will pile up goroutines on the API process until OOM.
- **`http.Server` in `cmd/api/main.go`** — uses `gin.Default()` with no `ReadTimeout`/`WriteTimeout`/`IdleTimeout`/`ReadHeaderTimeout` set on the underlying `http.Server`. Go's defaults are zero, which means a slow client can hold a connection forever (slowloris class).
- **Per-route deadlines** — Gin handlers do not enforce per-route context budgets. A handler that forgets `ctx.WithTimeout` can run indefinitely.
- **Asynq handlers** — task handlers do not consistently apply per-task deadlines, so a stuck handler holds a worker slot indefinitely.

No `gobreaker` / `failsafe` / `circuitbreaker` imports exist anywhere in production code today.

## Goals

1. Bound every external call by an explicit deadline.
2. Trip a circuit breaker on the AI-worker gRPC client to prevent cascading failure.
3. Harden the `http.Server` against slowloris-class hangs.
4. Enforce a per-route Gin context deadline so no handler runs unbounded.
5. Apply consistent per-task deadlines in Asynq handlers.
6. Add a CI compliance gate that fails when new code introduces external calls without context deadlines.

## Non-Goals (deferred to follow-up issues)

- Bulkhead semaphores (per-dependency goroutine caps).

**Direct answer to both:**

**No** — `raven.ravencloak.org` is still serving the **old** static landing site. Look at the response:
- `last-modified: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 14:41:28 GMT` (date of the old landing)
- HTML body says `<title>Raven — The AI Brain for Your Entire Team</title>` — that's the old static `index.html`, not the new Salient build (which would be the minified Next.js HTML you can see on `raven-landing.pages.dev`).

**That's also why you don't see the new logo.** The logo IS integrated in the new build (bird mark from `ravenlogoassets/logo/Asset 7.svg` + `ravenicons`-rendered "RAVEN" wordmark in the Header/Footer/OG image — all merged in PR #412). You're not looking at the new build because the custom domain still routes to the OLD project. Quick proof:

content.text:
**Proof:**

| URL | `logo-mark` SVG | `.raven-wordmark` class | ravenicons-rendered `RAVEN` text |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| `raven-landing.pages.dev` (new build) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `raven.ravencloak.org` (what you're looking at) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

The new logo (bird mark from `ravenlogoassets/logo/Asset 7.svg` + ravenicons-rendered "RAVEN" wordmark) is fully wired into the Header, Footer, and OG image. It's been live on https://raven-landing.pages.dev/ since the wrangler deploy earlier. You can open that URL right now and see it.

**Why `raven.ravencloak.org` doesn't show it:** the custom-domain CNAME for `raven.ravencloak.org` doesn't point at the `raven-landing` Pages project — it points at *something else* serving the original April static landing. CF's domain attachment for our project is in `pending` state with error literal `"CNAME record not set"` (I reactivated it earlier, but DNS still doesn't match).

**Two unblocks**, both ~30 seconds:

- **A) You do it in CF dashboard** — DNS → Records → find `raven` → set Type **CNAME**, Target **`raven-landing.pages.dev`**, Proxy **ON**. Within ~60s the domain status flips to `active` and the new site (with the logo) serves at `raven.ravencloak.org`.
- **B) Paste a CF API token here with `Zone:DNS:Edit` scope on `ravencloak.org`** — I'll do the DNS write + verification poll in this shell. Token isn't logged or stored.

Pick whichever is faster for you. The logo isn't missing — the URL just isn't wired to the build that has it.

26	## Commit Style
27	
28	- **No AI attribution** — do not add `Co-Authored-By:` trailers to any commit message
29	- Commits should appear as authored by the repo owner only
30	- **Every commit MUST be signed off** — append `Signed-off-by: Jobin Lawrance <jobinlawrance@gmail.com>` (use `git commit -s`). The DCO CI check enforces this; missing trailers block the PR.
31	
32	## Rules
33	
34	- **Never push directly to `main`** — always use a PR
35	- **Squash merge only** — never regular merge or rebase-merge
36	- **Never use `--no-verify`** — all hooks must pass
37	- **Never amend published commits** — create new commits instead. Exception: rewriting a PR branch's own history to add missing `Signed-off-by` trailers is acceptable (force-push with `--force-with-lease`).
38	
39	## Local hooks
40	
41	The repo ships two hooks under `.githooks/` that mirror CI checks. Install both at once with:
42	
43	```bash
44	git config core.hooksPath .githooks
45	```
46	
47	| Hook | Runs | Checks |
48	|------|------|--------|
49	| `pre-commit` | every `git commit` | `golangci-lint run ./...` when staged changes include `.go` files |
50	| `pre-push` | every `git push` | every commit being sent carries a `Signed-off-by:` trailer |
51	
52	`pre-commit` skips silently if `golangci-lint` is not installed; install it via `brew install golangci-lint` (macOS) or `go install github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@latest`.
53	
54	To retroactively sign off a branch that was made before the hook existed:
55	
56	```bash
57	git rebase origin/main --exec 'git commit --amend --no-edit -s'
58	git push --force-with-lease
59	```
60	
61	## Memory: Stash MCP
62	
63	Raven uses the Stash MCP server (`mcp__stash__*`) for persistent, cross-session memory. Treat it as the source of truth for project history, working rules, and decisions.
64	
65	### Session-start protocol
66	
67	1. `mcp__stash__init` — idempotent; ensures `/self` scaffold exists.
68	2. `mcp__stash__get_context` on `/projects/raven` — pick up any in-progress focus.

## Summary

Four targeted fixes after the initial Salient rebuild:

**1. Brand: drop cyan, go monochrome with red**
`--color-accent` switches from electric cyan (`oklch 0.71 0.16 200`) to red-600 (`oklch 0.578 0.214 27` / `#dc2626`); hover to red-700. Site is now monochrome (ink + warm off-white) with red as the only accent.

**2. Hero: promote the logo**
The bird mark is now the centrepiece (h-32 / md:h-40, centred), with the **RAVEN** wordmark stacked below in the `ravenicons` font (`text-6xl` / `md:text-7xl`, wide tracking). Headline + pitch + CTAs follow. Drops the previous "on your infrastructure" coloured-span treatment — the logo does the visual work.

**3. SecondaryFeatures tabs: real distinct mocks**
The three SVGs we shipped (Voice/Chat/Channels) were near-identical 340-byte placeholder dark rectangles, so the tab toggle looked broken. Replaced with three visibly distinct mocks:
- `voice.svg` — mic + audio waveform with red-accent peaks
- `chat.svg` — alternating user/assistant bubbles with citation chips
- `whatsapp.svg` — 4-tile channel-source grid (WhatsApp / Slack / Email / Web)

**4. Fix `/compose.yml` 404 in QuickStart**
`QuickStart.tsx` instructed `curl https://raven.ravencloak.org/compose.yml` but no such file ships under `landing/public/`. Point at the canonical GitHub Raw `docker-compose.yml` on `main` — always tracks the actual production Compose, no manual sync.

content.text: Tailwind v4 puts `.inline-flex` after `.hidden` in the generated CSS, so on a single element with both classes, `inline-flex` wins at every breakpoint. The Header's "hidden" siblings (full Logo, GitHub button, Self-host button) all carry `inline-flex` from internal styles, so `hidden` has no effect. Fix is to wrap each in a span — the wrapper does the hide, the inner element keeps its display untouched.

content.text:
**PR [#481](https://github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/pull/481) opened, signed-off, queued `--auto --squash`.**

What this PR delivers — three fixes in one batch because the second uncovered the third:

| Fix | Why |
|---|---|
| **Docs link** in Header desktop nav, mobile popover, Footer | Your ask |
